prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key pledges and plans (ideological framing removed)

- Tax, pensions and families
  - Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
  - Introduce Triple Lock Plus: uprate both State Pension and a new age-related personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; maintain current pension tax rules and benefits.
  - Childcare: 30 hours a week free from 9 months to school; expand Family Hubs nationwide.
  - Child Benefit to be assessed on household income, tapering from £120,000 to £160,000.
  - Raise at least £6bn/year by tackling tax avoidance/evasion.

- Welfare and work
  - Reform disability benefits (PIP) and work capability assessments; move fit notes to specialist work/health professionals.
  - Tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete move to Universal Credit; new Fraud Bill. Targeted welfare reforms to save £12bn/year.

- Business, regulation and government efficiency
  - Retain full expensing; explore extending to leasing; no rise in corporation tax. Ten-point SME plan (business rates relief, VAT threshold smoothing, Open Finance, reporting cuts, prompt payment, access to finance, SME-focused procurement, £250m Invest in Women Fund).
  - Reduce civil service to pre-pandemic size; halve consultancy spend; 2% annual productivity plans across departments.

- Infrastructure, innovation and trade
  - Redirect £36bn HS2 savings to regional transport; £8.3bn for potholes; nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in populated areas; automated vehicles framework.
  - Public R&D to £22bn/year; compute clusters (£1.5bn); £4.5bn for advanced manufacturing; expand Catapults.
  - Conclude FTAs (India, GCC); implement CPTPP; maintain standards in trade.

- Defence, security and foreign policy
  - Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; ≥£10bn for UK munitions; increase defence R&D (5% + 2% exploitation); National Defence and Resilience Plan; Veterans Bill and support package.

- Immigration and borders
  - Legal annual cap on work/family visas that falls each year; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks and higher IHS/insurance where needed.
  - Rwanda removals; clear asylum claims in six months; more returns deals; pursue international asylum reforms.

- Education and youth
  - Advanced British Standard (replace A/T Levels), English and maths to 18; mobile phone ban in schools; two hours of PE weekly.
  - 100,000 additional apprenticeships funded by closing low‑outcome degrees.
  - Mandatory National Service at 18: 12‑month military placements (competitive, paid) or 25 days civic service.

- NHS and social care
  - Real-terms funding growth; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgery builds/modernisations; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
  - Dental Recovery Plan; service commitments for newly qualified dentists.
  - Patient choice across NHS, charity and independent providers at NHS tariffs.
  - £3.4bn tech plan (NHS App front door, AI, Federated Data Platform); reduce managers by 5,500; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health measures; implement Cass Review; expand mental health support.

- Policing and justice
  - 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law.
  - Tougher sentences for serious offenders; new offences (spiking, deepfakes, intimate images); four new prisons; court modernisation; anti‑fraud measures.
  - Stronger protest-related public order powers.

- Energy, climate and environment
  - Annual North Sea licensing; windfall tax to 2028‑29 (with allowances); new gas power stations as backup.
  - Treble offshore wind; deliver CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new nuclear at Wylfa; streamline nuclear approvals.
  - £1.1bn Green Industries Growth Accelerator; import carbon pricing by 2027.
  - Keep energy levies lower than 2023; maintain price cap; review standing charges; £6bn for home efficiency plus universal vouchers; onshore wind with local consent; more rooftop/brownfield solar; no fracking.
  - Plan for Water (tougher enforcement, river restoration, price review reform); tree/peatland and urban greening; 11th National Park; 15‑minute access to nature goal; tougher waste crime penalties; limit new incinerators.

- Housing and local growth
  - 1.6m homes; end nutrient neutrality with mitigation fee to unlock ~100,000 homes; fast‑track brownfield in 20 largest cities; higher densities in inner London; urban development corporations.
  - Protect Green Belt; Infrastructure Levy for local services.
  - First-time buyer Stamp Duty relief up to £425k made permanent; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loan, 5% deposit); extend Mortgage Guarantee.
  - Two-year CGT relief for landlords selling to sitting tenants; complete leasehold reform (ground rent cap → peppercorn, end unfair forfeiture, promote commonhold); Renters Reform Bill (abolish Section 21 with court reform; stronger ASB grounds); manage holiday lets; rough sleeping measures.

- Communities, transport, culture and sport
  - £20m endowments for 105 towns (plus more); extend Shared Prosperity Fund; more Freeports/Investment Zones.
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban local road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for new 20mph/Low Traffic Neighbourhoods; extend £2 bus fare cap for full Parliament; National Parking Platform; GBR rail reform and nationwide PAYG contactless.
  - Continue grassroots sports investment; Independent Football Regulator; maintain competitive creative tax reliefs; BBC funding and complaints reform.

- Equality, online safety, sex and gender
  - Clarify Equality Act: sex means biological sex; single legal sex; parental rights on school decisions; proceed cautiously on conversion practices legislation.
  - Online Safety Act enforcement; statutory school mobile bans; consult on stronger parental controls.

- Farming, fisheries and rural
  - Increase UK farming budget by £1bn over Parliament (inflation‑linked); ringfence devolved shares; legal food security target and UK Food Security Index; 50% public food spend local/higher standard; fast‑track farm infrastructure; five‑year tapered Seasonal Worker scheme; replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund; support inshore fleets; rural broadband/transport/housing; maintain flood defence funding.

- Union and devolution
  - Comparable public service data across the UK; protect internal market; extend Shared Prosperity Fund and town endowments to devolved nations; support devolved Freeports/EIZ; implement Windsor Framework and NI measures; targeted commitments for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland on transport, energy and industry.
